---
title: "Health Domains & Machine Learning: A Skill-Building Course"
---

## Welcome

This site hosts a self-paced series of **15 lessons**. Each lesson pairs a distinct **health domain** with a distinct **statistical or machine-learning model**, walking you from domain context to a runnable practical exercise.

Every lesson follows the same scaffold:

1. **Introduction to the Domain** — what the problem is and why it matters.
2. **Research Question** — a concrete, answerable question.
3. **Open-Source Dataset** — a publicly available data source, with discussion and a link.
4. **Practical Exercise** — which model/framework to explore, starter code, suggested AI prompts, and extension ideas.

## How to use this course

- Work the lessons **in order** the first time through; later you can jump to a domain or model of interest.
- Each exercise is designed to be completed in a Jupyter notebook or RStudio session; starter code is provided.
- Use the suggested **AI prompts** to have a language model explain, debug, or extend your analysis — treat the AI as a tutor, not an oracle.
- Datasets are linked, not vendored: download them yourself so you control versioning.

## Prerequisites

- Basic Python (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn) or R.
- A GitHub account if you want to fork and track your own progress.
- Curiosity about health data and responsible ML.

## Responsible use

Health data carries real-world consequences. Models built in these exercises are **educational** and must not be used for clinical decision-making. Always validate on independent data, examine fairness across subgroups, and involve domain experts.
